scenarioPanels.caption: A hospital holds sensitive patient records that must be available to authorised staff at all hours.
Staff reach the server remotely from hospital-issued smartphones and laptops over authenticated connections.
On-call doctors retrieve records from outside the hospital and make faster clinical decisions for patients.
The same remote pathway widens the attack surface against the hospital's records.
A lost device or phished credentials let an attacker authenticate to the server as if they were a legitimate user.
A confidentiality breach becomes notifiable under UK GDPR, exposing the hospital to ICO regulatory action and reputational damage.

phrases.text: One positive impact is continuous availability of patient records for authorised staff.
Because the server is reachable from hospital-issued smartphones and laptops, on-call doctors can retrieve patient records remotely instead of needing to be physically present.
Faster clinical decisions in time-critical situations, like an on-call consultant reviewing patient history, improve outcomes and meet the hospital's continuous-availability requirement.
One negative impact is increased exposure to cyber attacks on the server holding sensitive medical information.
Lost or stolen devices and phishing-compromised credentials let attackers authenticate to the server like an authorised user.
A confidentiality breach would be a notifiable data breach under UK GDPR, exposing the hospital to ICO regulatory action and reputational damage.

positive.introduce: One positive impact for the hospital is that authorised staff can access patient records at any time, including when they are away from the hospital site.
positive.explain: Because the server is reachable over the internet from hospital-issued smartphones and laptops, on-call doctors and specialists responding from outside the hospital can retrieve sensitive medical information when they need it, rather than being blocked by having to be physically present at a workstation.
positive.develop: This means the hospital can make faster clinical decisions in time-critical situations, for example when an on-call consultant reviews a patient's medical history before authorising treatment, which improves patient outcomes and helps the hospital meet its requirement for continuous availability of records.

negative.introduce: One negative impact is that allowing access over the internet increases the hospital's exposure to cyber attacks on the server holding sensitive medical information.
negative.explain: Each smartphone and laptop that can reach the server becomes a potential entry point for an attacker, so if a device is lost or stolen, or if a member of staff's credentials are compromised through phishing, the attacker can authenticate to the server in the same way an authorised user would.
negative.develop: This creates the risk of a confidentiality breach affecting patient medical records, which would be a notifiable data breach under UK GDPR and could expose the hospital to regulatory action from the Information Commissioner's Office and significant reputational damage that undermines patient trust in how their data is handled.

scenarioPanels.caption: A national retailer receives over 80,000 graduate-role applications a year and the recruitment team cannot read every CV.
An AI screening tool scores each application against criteria derived from the past five years of successful hires.
Recruiters receive a ranked shortlist and focus their time on engaging top candidates rather than reading every CV.
The training data reflects who was hired before, so any historical preference for one demographic shows up as a learned scoring rule.
Applicants from protected groups are scored lower for reasons unrelated to merit, never reaching the human-review stage.
Indirect discrimination under Equality Act 2010 s.19 plus a solely-automated decision restricted by UK GDPR Article 22: two simultaneous statutory exposures.

phrases.text: One positive impact for the retailer is the operational efficiency of automated CV screening at scale.
Because AI can sift through tens of thousands of applications in minutes against the same scoring criteria, the recruitment team is freed from the most time-consuming part of the early funnel.

This lets recruiters spend more time on shortlisted-candidate engagement and reduces the time-to-hire, both of which improve the retailer's competitiveness for talent and the candidate experience for those who progress.
One negative impact is the risk of indirect discrimination against applicants in protected groups.

AI trained on the retailer's historical hiring data inherits patterns of who has been hired before, so any historical preference for one demographic over another shows up as a learned scoring rule that disadvantages similar candidates today.

This creates simultaneous exposure under the Equality Act 2010 (likely indirect discrimination under section 19, since the screening rule applies uniformly but disadvantages protected groups) and under the UK GDPR (Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects on data subjects, with required safeguards including human review and the right to challenge).

positive.introduce: One positive impact for the retailer is the operational efficiency of automated CV screening at scale.
positive.explain: Because the AI can sift through tens of thousands of applications in minutes against the same scoring criteria, the recruitment team is freed from the most time-consuming part of the early funnel and is no longer the bottleneck.
positive.develop: This lets recruiters spend more time on shortlisted-candidate engagement, reduces the time-to-hire, and produces a more consistent applicant experience for those who progress, all of which improve the retailer's competitiveness for talent.

negative.introduce: One negative impact is the risk of indirect discrimination against applicants in protected groups.
negative.explain: AI trained on the retailer's historical hiring data inherits the patterns of who has been hired before, so any historical preference for one demographic over another, even one that was unintentional, shows up as a learned scoring rule that disadvantages similar candidates today.
negative.develop: This creates simultaneous exposure under two Acts. Under the Equality Act 2010 it is likely to be indirect discrimination under section 19, because the screening rule applies uniformly but puts protected groups at a particular disadvantage. Under the UK GDPR, Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects on data subjects, requiring safeguards such as meaningful human review and a right to challenge the outcome.
